bug_semantics: In both github-issue-bot templates, verifyWebhook returns `typeof signature !== 'string' || await verify(...)`. A request with no `X-Hub-Signature-256` header makes the first operand true and short-circuits HMAC verification. The caller rejects only a false return, so the unsigned request is accepted; an attacker-controlled `repository` and `issue` from the JSON body then reach `postComment`, which uses the configured GITHUB_TOKEN to create a comment on the selected repository and issue.
flaw_origin: Commit 7840536b88784d791ee19461ff091528d6fb5b81 extracted the old inline rejection predicate `missing signature || verified signature` from main.js into a new method named verifyWebhook, returned that predicate unchanged, and changed main.js to reject only `!verifyWebhook(req)`. This semantic inversion converted `missing signature` from a rejection case in the direct parent into a successful verification result. The later TypeScript template commit 4d69364b6a5b9aa1e0d8d9a66c4914b341480718 copied the already-flawed contract but did not originate it.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object identifies author and committer as loks0n (Luke B. Silver; non-bot GitHub user), with identical authored/committed timestamps; its complete message is only `fix: esm migration`, its body is empty, and it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, Copilot, or other attribution trailer.
evidence: Advisory and attack path: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-785c-v4m5-q4wg names node/github-issue-bot/src/github.js, node-typescript/github-issue-bot/src/github.ts, and the negating caller, and reports affected and patched versions as Unknown. The first-party report https://github.com/appwrite/templates/issues/350 (still open) reproduces the missing-header short circuit.

BIC patch: https://github.com/appwrite/templates/commit/7840536b88784d791ee19461ff091528d6fb5b81 shows github-issue-bot/src/github.js gaining verifyWebhook with `return (typeof signature !== 'string' || await verify(...))` while github-issue-bot/src/main.js changes from an inline rejecting `if (missing || verify)` to `if (!(await github.verifyWebhook(req)))`. The full commit object at https://github.com/appwrite/templates/commit/7840536b88784d791ee19461ff091528d6fb5b81.json gives the sole parent 59fa20b14997f155cd0980cf50579977b2ccdfc9, human author/committer loks0n, and an empty body/no trailers.

Direct-parent verification: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/appwrite/templates/59fa20b14997f155cd0980cf50579977b2ccdfc9/github-issue-bot/src/github.js has no verifyWebhook method. In https://raw.githubusercontent.com/appwrite/templates/59fa20b14997f155cd0980cf50579977b2ccdfc9/github-issue-bot/src/main.js the missing-signature operand is inside the 401 rejection condition, so an absent header is rejected rather than accepted. Thus the vulnerable return contract and missing-header acceptance path are absent from the direct parent tree.

File history traces through that move to 7840536b88784d791ee19461ff091528d6fb5b81. The TypeScript copy was added later by https://github.com/appwrite/templates/commit/4d69364b6a5b9aa1e0d8d9a66c4914b341480718, whose parent is 954c0c09cfc7 and whose patch creates node-typescript/github-issue-bot/src/github.ts with the same flawed return.

There is consequently no fix commit, direct fix, or patched release to cite as of the audited repository state.

reasoning: The vulnerability-first trace distinguishes the expression's meaning from its text. In parent 59fa20b14997f155cd0980cf50579977b2ccdfc9, `typeof signature !== 'string' || verify(...)` is an inline rejection guard, so a missing header yields 401. BIC 7840536b88784d791ee19461ff091528d6fb5b81 moves the same predicate into verifyWebhook as a positive return value and negates only at the caller; this is the smallest commit that first makes a missing signature authenticate successfully. Later refactors, the 100% rename, and the TypeScript copy preserve or replicate that mechanism rather than originate it. The direct parent lacks the vulnerable positive-return contract, the BIC precedes tag 0.1.0, and both boundary tags 0.1.0 and 1.1.2 are vulnerable. Current main is identical to 1.1.2, the first-party issue remains open, and the advisory lists no patched version, so the case is demonstrably unpatched and both fix fields are null. Applying the required BIC-only attribution rule, the BIC object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, yielding NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched: no remediation commit or patched version exists in the audited public history through main/tag 1.1.2 (dcb00987a777afb3d29f20ea8023070c30e6a949), so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha necessarily remain null.

unpatched.reason: No remediation commit or patched version exists in the audited public history through main/tag 1.1.2 (dcb00987a777afb3d29f20ea8023070c30e6a949).

potential_fix.approach: Verify the webhook HMAC signature with a constant-time comparison over the raw request body against the configured template secret, rejecting missing or non-string signatures.
potential_fix.rationale: Authentic signature verification prevents forged webhook deliveries from triggering template actions.
